listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Thursday, November 5. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is from Georgia. Democrats have won control of the Georgia House of Representatives for the first time in 22 years. That is according to reporting from the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, relayed by Rough Draft Atlanta. The win was part of a so-called blue wave that has transformed Georgia's politics overnight. Democrats swept the top seats. Fuller results should come in over the next few days. Now the front page. In Hong Kong, activist Joshua Wong has been jailed for ten years. He is thirty years old. He is one of hundreds of people detained under the national security law. In football, Brandon Aiyuk has filed to be reinstated. His agent says he plans to report to the San Francisco 49ers on Friday. In architecture technology, Qonic has launched AI agents inside its BIM platform. They let users find, check, fix and create BIM data using plain language. Now the sections. In tech and AI, Anthropic says it is committing a portion of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund. Also, a trending tool called claude-mem stores what an agent does and feeds context back into later sessions. In politics, NPR's morning brief covers Democratic agenda planning and ballots still being counted in some races. The Lever reports that voters in deep-red areas approved a plan to ban corporate political spending. In world news, Kyiv says bodycam video shows a double-tap Russian bombing of a village that killed at least forty people. Separately, the BBC reports unusually wild typhoon weather across East Asia, linked to El Niño. In sports, the Houston Rockets lost to the Minnesota Timberwolves, one hundred seventeen to one hundred seven. Kyle Shanahan says Jauan Jennings told him he is happy with the Vikings. And Atlanta's Matt Olson won his fourth Gold Glove. In Atlanta, a Microsoft-backed pocket park in East Point has set its official opening date. The Atlanta Regional Commission also launched a major economic mobility effort called Opportunity Rising. In architecture, Mach9 added aerial LiDAR and photogrammetry support to its AI CAD software. AEC Magazine also has a Q and A on making AI-built software safe and accountable. In science and nature, NASA unveiled a new experimental aircraft called the X-70 Fractal. NASA leaders also shared plans for returning Americans to the Moon in 2028. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Report: Democrats take Georgia House of Representatives
lead.note: Democrats have won control of the Georgia House of Representatives for the first time in 22 years. The report comes from Rough Draft Atlanta, which cites reporting by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. The outcome was part of what the summary calls a so-called blue wave. That wave, it says, has transformed Georgia's politics overnight, with Democrats sweeping the top seats. For a reader in Atlanta, the change matters because the state House is where much of the state's legislation is shaped, and control of the chamber has not changed hands in more than two decades. The item is a short report and is attributed to the newspaper, so details such as seat counts are not given here. It is worth following as fuller results and analysis come in over the coming days.
